name: Planetarium / Eno-style ambient space pad on any synth: sines at 0, +12 and +19 semitones, a triangle sub, two slow free-running smooth-random LFOs that modulate each other's rate and are mixed on every target, low-sustain amp envelope, gentle filter, and LFO-moved reverb/delay mix
goal: Build the classic slow 'space / planetarium / Brian Eno' meditation pad from an init patch on any synth with three oscillators, two LFOs and a reverb and delay. Everything moves a little, and no two parameters move together, so the ear never locks onto a pattern. Pitch stays steady: all movement is in level, timbre and effect mix.

source.title: How to make an ambient space pad in any synth.  Sound Design Tutorial 1

prerequisites: Any synth (VST, hardware or Web Audio) with at least three oscillators plus a sub/noise source, two or three LFOs with free-run and smooth-random shapes, a low-pass/band-pass filter, reverb and delay
Basic idea of LFO depth and bipolar/unipolar modulation

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Note or key to play the pad in (white-key improvisation works)

inputs.name: background_noise
inputs.description: Optional consistent natural bed (rain, wind, forest, spaceship hum) mixed very low

outputs.name: pad_audio
outputs.description: Long held-chord render with slow, non-repeating movement

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Keep all modulation subtle. If the listener notices a movement, it is too much.
Do not use LFO-driven big filter sweeps on the pad. If you want a sweep, put it on a send/aux filter and use it sparingly.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): do not modulate oscillator pitch or delay time, except at most a tiny fine-time amount. Keep unison detune motion slight.
Keep delay stereo spread low on pads (save wide ping-pong for sharp arps or percussion).
Keep any background noise bed consistent and natural (rain and birdsong together sounds wrong).

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: OscillatorNodes + GainNodes for layers, BiquadFilterNode for filters, ConvolverNode/feedback DelayNode for reverb/delay, slow custom LFOs (ConstantSource + smoothed random) on AudioParams.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Init the patch and set the oscillators to sine waves: osc 1 at 0 st, osc 2 at +12 st (one octave), osc 3 at +19 st (an octave and a fifth).
steps.expect: Organ-like stack; the +19 adds a faint fifth on top

steps.action: Set up two LFOs: rate in Hz (not tempo-synced) and very slow, smooth-random shape (random but gliding, not stepped), free-running so they do not restart on each key, bipolar.
steps.expect: Slow wandering control signals that keep going across notes

steps.action: Cross-modulate the LFOs: send a small amount of LFO 3 to the rate of LFO 2, and of LFO 2 to the rate of LFO 3.
steps.expect: The two LFOs never move in lockstep

steps.action: Modulate the level of the +12 osc with LFO 3 and the +19 osc with LFO 2, plus a smaller amount on osc 1 (the root should move least). On every target, mix a bit of both LFOs, sometimes inverted.
steps.expect: Upper partials fade gently in and out, like a slow chorus

steps.action: Add a sub oscillator one octave down using a triangle wave (square is too buzzy with sines). Add a trace of noise (pink, white or blue) for high-end character, barely audible.
steps.expect: Body underneath and faint air on top, no buzz

steps.action: Amp envelope: long attack, long decay, sustain lowered (sloping down), long release.
steps.expect: Overlapping notes die back instead of piling up into mud

steps.action: Low-pass filter for roundness with low resonance. Move cutoff only slightly with the LFOs.
steps.expect: Slightly rounder tone; no audible sweep or resonant peak

steps.action: Effects: a big cathedral-type reverb and a delay. Put both LFOs, mixed, on reverb dry/wet, delay dry/wet and delay feedback, but not on delay time. Low-cut the effects returns to avoid mud.
steps.expect: The space breathes in and out; low end stays clean

steps.action: Turn on unison on the oscillators (several voices) with only slight LFO movement, then stop adding things. Save the patch, take a 5-15 minute break and come back for small balance tweaks.
steps.expect: Choir-like thickness; the patch is done before it gets overloaded

steps.action: Optional: add shimmer reverb tuned to +7 st (a fifth) instead of the default octave, with its mix moved slowly in and out.
steps.expect: Soft shimmer that does not get grating when notes are held

steps.action: Optional: add a low-level consistent noise bed (rain, metallic flow, forest) through a slow, subtle band-pass in parallel with the main filter. Add slow LFO on overall volume and pan, plus small EQ dips on any resonant buildup (not many narrow cuts, which cause a comb-filter effect).
steps.expect: Context bed under the pad without screeching resonances

verification: No two modulated parameters rise and fall together over a 60 s listen.
Pitch is steady: no audible vibrato or detune wobble beyond light unison.
Holding overlapping chords for 30 s does not build up low-mid mud (sustain is below max and FX returns are low-cut).
Reverb and delay mix audibly breathe over about 20-60 s cycles.
